* OSS is too far behind to catch up

* All software will be replaced by agents

* You can’t build moats on top of models

* You don’t need evals

* RAG is dead 

* AI will decimate engineering jobs

* Prompting won’t matter in the future 

* We’ve hit a training wall

* Frontier models are too dangerous to release 

…and dozens and dozens more. The key here is to remain flexible in your thinking because we’re going to be in a constant state of change for a while.

tweets.text:
AI product building has a ~3-month playbook half-life. Here’s how to adapt.

Most trad product teams are built to discover a playbook and then milk it for the next 5 years.

However in the AI labs, we consciously throw away playbooks every few months cos we start seeing diminishing returns.

Here’s what you can do as an AI builder:

Focus on defining a set of meta-principles for 
1/ how you continuously learn what the market wants today and what it might want in 3 months
2/ how you execute with extreme urgency

The specifics of 1 and 2 will vary based on your domain and product type.
Build a team that learns and adapts at that pace. 

Legacy teams are optimized for playbook milking.

AI teams need to be optimized for inventing.

You rarely get to see this level of personal drama in crypto.

Somehow Justin Sun has delivered a story involving a Chinese movie star, private jets, a $50 million demand, surrogacy, Claude AI, a lawsuit — and now CZ has entered the chat.

Here’s what happened.

@justinsuntron says he first became obsessed with Chinese actress Jing Tian in 2007, when he was still a University student.

Sun says he kept an old blurry photo of her on every phone and computer he owned for the next 19 years. Then, almost two decades later, they actually got together.

And this is where the story gets ridiculous.

Sun describes buying out an entire cinema so they could watch Zootopia 2 alone. People who had already bought tickets were reportedly met outside and paid cash to leave.

He says they flew around on private jets, travelled from Tenerife to the Maldives, and stayed surrounded by assistants, security and hotel staff.

Then things got serious. Sun proposed in the Maldives in January.

He transferred $4.5 million to accounts belonging to Jing’s parents as a bride price.

That part has now spilled into an actual lawsuit. Sun is suing Jing and her parents to recover the money.

But the truly insane part comes next.

According to Sun’s essay, they were planning to have a child through a surrogate.

A 34-year-old surrogate in California had apparently already been selected. A $200,000 deposit had been paid.

Jing then travelled to California for an egg retrieval. Sun says he booked an entire floor of Montage Laguna Beach for 30 days at a cost of $1 million to protect her privacy.

On the eighth day, she called him. Her price to continue, according to Sun: $50 MILLION.

Sun could afford it. He says he literally ran his liquid assets through Claude Code and confirmed paying $50 million would barely affect him.

Then he asked Claude whether he should do it.

Claude’s answer: “Do not give her the fifty million dollars.”

Sun then asked the AI whether Jing no longer loved him.

Claude essentially replied that it neither understood nor cared about love — but he still shouldn’t send the money.

The next day Jing called again. She asked whether he had decided.

Sun stayed silent for 11 seconds.
She said: “I understand” and hung up.

Sun says he never saw her again.

After writing thousands of words filled with incredibly specific names, payments, hotels, planes and conversations, Sun ends the essay by saying: 

“This work is entirely fictional. Any resemblance to real people or events is purely coincidental.”

Jing has now responded publicly: “I will never sell my love for money, nor would I ever sell my soul.”

And now Binance founder CZ entered the scene.

His message to Sun was basically: take the money dispute to court if you need to — but stop turning someone’s private life into a public marketing campaign.

Crypto has produced plenty of billionaire feuds. But there’s never been one involving a famous actress, a surrogate, a $50 million ultimatum, and Claude AI acting as the relationship therapist.

今晚的加密市场，大概率系于沃什同志的嘴上。

美东上午 10 点（今晚 22:00），美联储主席凯文·沃什将在杰克逊霍尔 （Jackson Hole ）发表核心讲话。

这个名字听着像个偏远的洞，但它其实是全球央行行长的“达沃斯论坛”。每年 8 月，美联储及全球顶尖宏观大佬都会齐聚怀俄明州的这个山谷。

历史上，美联储极其喜欢在这个年会上“搞突袭”，定调未来半年的货币政策。

目前，Polymarket 上，针对 9 月利率决议的押注比例是

70% 的概率认为保持不变，即暂停加息；29% 的资金押注“加息 25 个基点”，仅有约 1% 押注降息。

所以今晚的剧本如果偏鸽（符合 70% 预期）： 释放不加息信号，靴子落地，大盘更大概率向上突破

偏鹰（触发 29% 预期）： 态度强硬超预期利空，加密或许先跌为敬。

短线选手最怕沃什同志打太极，态度模糊的话那更可能是熟悉的画门行情。

一枚比特币的价格，八万两千美金。

通向牛来的路，卡在了这周。

吃瓜和学习孙哥写作之余，有没有注意到 bitcoin:native 这周总是一摸到82K就精准回落？

一个可能会影响 BTC 后市的变量很多人没咋关注，那就是期权市场。

海外分析师 @ThePenguinBTC 给出了一个现货价格背后、大多数人没太关注的期权博弈视角，把这几天的行情震荡逻辑讲的非常明白：

BTC 目前正被夹在一个“期权铁桶”里。

- 上方阻力（8.2 万）： 巨鲸们在这个位置卖出了大量看涨期权收权利金。
作为对手盘的市场做市商，为了对冲风险，只要价格一靠近 8.2 万，就会被动在现货市场卖出 BTC。这就是为什么每次冲高都会被精准砸下来。

-下方支撑（7.5 万）： 同样的逻辑反过来。巨鲸卖出看跌期权，做市商为了对冲，在价格靠近 7.5 万时会被动买入。

-重灾区（8 万）： 双方火力最集中的地方，导致 BTC 在这里反复拉锯了 3 天。

而在今天周五，这个“铁桶”格局将被彻底打破。

价值高达 64.4 亿美元（约占 Deribit 未平仓头寸五分之一）的 81,700 份 BTC 期权，已于约 50 分钟前完成到期交割。

到期清算后，做市商在 8 万-8.2 万区间的“被动砸盘”任务就结束了，短期内上方的抛压阻力将消失。

而分析进一步指出，盘面的异动已经有资金在抢跑了；比如本周的看涨期权的权利金已经开始贵于看跌期权，甚至有大资金在提前布局 9 月 4 日 8.2 万上方的合约。

有个博主花 11 天刷完了油管 141 个投资视频，21 个频道，一只股票一只股票记下来。被反复点名的只剩 5 家：谷歌、英伟达、美光、CoreWeave、优步。

《大空头》主角原型 Eisman 看完这些的反应是直接卖掉谷歌。他的原话：「It's all just one trade，so it better succeed。」这是一笔交易，要么全赢，要么全输。

Brian 把 141 个视频的主题数了一遍：76 个在讲芯片、云、AI 模型，正好超过一半。你以为这 5 只是分散持仓，其实其中 4 只（谷歌、英伟达、美光、CoreWeave）是同一笔 AI 赌注穿了 4 个名字。连「唯一独立」的优步，它的风险（无人驾驶）也跑在英伟达的芯片上。

1/ 抄共识股清单，等于把分散做成假的 

141 个视频，76 个讲同一件事。如果你的自选股是从这类视频攒出来的，你持有的是 5 家公司还是 1 笔赌注穿了 5 个名字，值得翻出来看一遍。

Brian 自己承认 guilty：「我的清单也是这么攒的。」

2/ 谷歌现价 362 美元，便宜和贵同时成立，所以只开半仓定投 

按已赚到的利润算，谷歌是 10 年来最便宜的一档。按销售额算，是 10 年来最贵的 3%。同一只股票两个相反结论，差别只在看财报哪一行。巴菲特的伯克希尔刚翻倍加仓进持仓前三。

Brian 的做法：半仓+按月定投，不重仓。有博主直播做过实验：先问观众多少价位卖谷歌，公布巴菲特加仓消息后再问，所有人全改口。一条新闻就能让你丢掉自己的规矩。

3/ 英伟达估值说便宜三分之一，违约保险在翻倍 

有博主拿 Excel 算出每股值 300 美元，现价 221 美元，看起来便宜了四分之一以上。但客户们借了 5,000 亿美元买芯片，接近英伟达年营收两倍，债务违约保险从 5 月底以来翻倍。

Brian 自己算 290 美元，但仓位已到 12%上限。148 美元以下他坚决不接：真跌到那里，是接飞刀。

4/ 美光的纪律最值得抄：961 是开关，434 是故事线 

合理价约 1,450 美元听起来空间巨大，但两个数字要一起看：按已实现利润 22 倍，按明年预期利润 6 倍。两个数同时成立的前提是市场默认利润翻 3 倍。周期股顶部恰恰经常看起来便宜。

他的操作：50 日均线 961 美元，跌破按计划继续买（一分不多加），站回线上才加码；跌到 434 美元说明公司坏了，之前的分析全部作废。

5/ CoreWeave 有 1300 亿订单，他一股不买 

1999 年的朗讯：借钱给客户，客户拿这钱买朗讯设备，朗讯记成自己的收入，客户破产后需求现原形。现在英伟达在 SEC 文件里同意租回 CoreWeave 到 2032 年租不出去的所有算力。结构上同一件事。

CoreWeave 上市才 17 个月，历史不够画阶梯，Brian 的整板表上这一行写着「站着看」。他强调：站着观望和持有是两码事。

6/ 优步是唯一不是 AI 赌注的一只，两个人独立算价只差 10 美元 

每年约 100 亿美元自由现金，市值 1,500 亿，10 年最便宜的三分之一。有博主独立算的合理价是 120 美元，Brian 自己算的是 109 美元，两人从没看过对方的工作，只差 5%。现价 67 美元。

担心的事只有一件：无人驾驶要么抢乘客，要么逼它自己养车队。Brian 给到整张表最深的买入档。

Eisman 那句话值得再放一遍：“It's all just one trade。”

5 只股票，1 笔 AI 赌注。买之前先想清楚：这个赌注要是输了，你的组合里还剩什么。

tweets.text: When agents cost cents a day, there will be billions of them... and all of them need somewhere to hold money and transact. That's the piece I published this week.  https://t.co/OFY6HExSsG

In the next two or three years, every human could have a hundred... maybe a thousand agents working for them onchain.

Arpan Nanavati breaks it down perfectly in this clip... the whole thing is a cost  curve.

Right now, it costs about $10 a day in inference to run an agent... hedge fund territory. But inference costs have already dropped 100x in three years, and every step down changes who can afford to play:

At $1 a day, every protocol is running agents

At cents a day, your wallet has agents built in, managing your idle capital

At microcents, you get agent swarms

Jevons paradox... every time the cost of something collapses, usage explodes. 

Intelligence is scaling, and theres no reason the number of agents executing onchain cant scale near infinitely.

Madness.

But it won't be just crypto valuations that break. GDP, productivity, inflation, the speed value gets created and destroyed... every gauge we have for measuring an economy assumes the economy moves at human speed. When it stops moving at human speed, the instruments stop working with it. I call it The Economic Singularity.

David Mattin and I dig into all of this every week in The Exponentialist. It lived inside Real Vision for years... now its own publication on Substack, with a free tier: https://t.co/uQ5cEw6MOo

i could go on and on about the little things, time, mirroring etc lmao. But you get the point

I mostly have two types of trades I take, one is a more defensive trade which depends on velocity into a HTF area, the other is reclaims. With a lot of weight into historical context. But the general idea is to trade around areas that when you are wrong, it's cheap to be wrong, but when you're right the upside is somewhat unlimited. On the ones when I'm right. I like to be a little more aggressive into adding into the trend early on to mid stage. Obviously there's other context like market structure, momentum, strength off or into an area. But in general, its my bread and butter setup. I still dabble and take other trades, sometimes around the core on LTF's. But that's essentially what I like. And there's obviously a lot of other things you look at like how price is responding to x narratives and if its strengthening or weakening into that. A lot of it is just gut, pattern recognition.
